# Deep Gaussian Processes for Financial Risk Modeling

GPs and DGPs have found widespread application across various domains, including regression, classification, and time series forecasting. In financial services, they are particularly well-suited for tasks like probability of default (PD) prediction, where accurate uncertainty quantification is crucial for risk management [**TODO: CITE**]. Regulations such as Basel III [**TODO: cite**] require financial institutions to hold capital reserves proportional to the risk of their loan portfolios, making precise PD estimates essential for compliance and profitability. In these models, risk and uncertainty often have direct financial implications [**TODO CITE!!!!**], so the ability of GPs and DGPs to provide calibrated uncertainty estimates, on top of competitive predictive performance, makes them an attractive choice for PD prediction. This analysis will compare the performance of standard GPs and DGPs against traditional machine learning methods on real-world financial datasets, and evaluate if the improved flexability of DGPs translates into better calibrated risk estimates and discriminative performance in practice.
